# Audit log management

This page covers recurring audit-log management. Initial log and event sink setup should be completed during installation or service onboarding.

## Audit

In HCP Terraform only, the <a href="https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cloud-docs/api-docs/audit-trails" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">Audit Trails API</a> provides access to audit events. We recommend Terraform Enterprise customers <a href="https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/enterprise/admin/infrastructure/logging" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">forward logs</a> for monitoring and auditing purposes. See the section on observability for more details.
Include audit, logging, and monitoring in the target architecture for the delivery of your project.  **Do not wait until after go-live to implement observability**.

## HCP Terraform audit trail logs

### HCP Terraform audit trail logs

HCP Terraform features an Audit Log API endpoint that you must use to collect the audit events and store them in the appropriate system. To implement this solution, you need the following.

- A method to schedule and automate the audit events collection,
- A secure storage solution to store the audit events, and
- A data lifecycle solution to correctly dispose of the audit events once they are no longer required.

<Warning>

HCP Terraform keeps audit trail records for 14 days and then discards it. Design and configure your audit trail collection solution for HCP Terraform with this in mind.

</Warning>

If you use a Security Information and Event Management system (SIEM), this must be the destination for those audit events. Suppose you are not using a SIEM but instead are using a centralized log management solution (Datadog, New Relic, Elastic, and so on). In that case, you must send those audit events to your centralized log management system. If neither of these solutions is available, still collect those audit events and store them securely using an object storage solution, such as AWS S3.

### Collection patterns

Choose the collection method based on your destination:

- **Splunk:** Use the <a href="https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cloud-docs/integrations/splunk" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">HCP Terraform for Splunk</a> app, which polls the Audit Trails API with an organization API token. This is the lowest-effort option when Splunk is your SIEM.
- **Other SIEMs and log platforms:** Poll the Audit Trails API on a schedule from a small, managed job (for example a serverless function or a cloud workflow service) and write the events to the destination. Manage the job itself as Terraform code, store the organization token in a secrets manager, and alert if the job stops, because any gap longer than the retention period is unrecoverable.

If you migrate to a new HCP Terraform organization, configure audit collection for the destination organization before you move workloads, so there is no gap in the audit record.
